children: Copper was set to end the week higher on Friday, as stronger physical demand in China helped withstand pressure from US tariff uncertainty and higher interest rates.
Three-month copper on the London Metal Exchange
rose 0.3% to $14,539 a metric ton, and was on track to end the week more than 2% higher.
The most-traded copper contract on the Shanghai Futures Exchange
closed 1.4% higher at 109,620 yuan  ($16,366.57) a ton, ending the week up 0.8%.
Signs of firmer physical buying in China have strengthened after copper retreated from record highs last week, helping offset headwinds from US policies.

Washington has yet to decide whether to impose tariffs on refined copper, Reuters reported last week, while the Federal Reserve raised rates by 25 basis points this week and indicated another increase could follow this year.

Copper's resilience was reflected in physical-market premiums. The Yangshan copper premium (SMM-CUYP-CN), a gauge of Chinese demand for imported copper, rose to $121 a ton on Thursday, its highest since October 2022. The premium has climbed from $85 at the end of last week.
The premium paid over SHFE copper (SMM-CU-PND) remained elevated at 630 yuan a ton on Thursday, slightly below 645 yuan the day earlier as the exchange prices recovered.

However, copper stocks in warehouses monitored by SHFE (CU-STX-SGH) rose 2.4% to 56,073 tons, according to the exchange's weekly stock report on Friday, after a three-week decline that had brought the inventories to their lowest since January 2024.

The LME tightness continued to ease, as stocks (MCUSTX-TOTAL) rose to 255,900 tons as of Wednesday and a near-term contango persisted, with the cash copper's discount against three-month (CMCU0-3) at $7.5 a ton.
Copper also benefited from softer oil prices. Easing concerns over Saudi supply disruptions outweighed fresh fighting between Saudi Arabia and Iran-backed Houthis in the Middle East. Brent crude
fell nearly 1% but remained above $100 a barrel.
LME aluminium
fell 0.2% and nickel
slipped 0.3%, while zinc
rose 0.5%, lead
gained 0.2% and tin
climbed 0.9%.
SHFE aluminium
rose 0.7%, zinc
advanced 1.6%, lead
gained 2.0%, nickel
added 1.0% and tin
climbed 2.0%.
($1 = 6.6978 Chinese yuan)
